note: The ASIA HARD-DATA PLANE. `deep_forest_sources.json` holds the PRACTITIONER forest -- 502 grounds where people say what they believe, which are hypothesis generators and never evidence. This file holds the other half: official, exchange, physical and flow data, where the number itself is the observation. The two are kept apart on purpose. A forum post and an SHFE warehouse receipt are both public Chinese information and they earn completely different treatment: one mints a hypothesis, the other can settle one. Adding a source here means declaring an MT5 transmission path for it -- a dataset with no path into a tradable instrument is not collected, however interesting, because trial count is a shared cost (LAWS: TWO LANES) and an unroutable feed spends it for nothing. REGION ROUTING RULE (principal, 2026-09-15), which has now held for China, Japan, SE Asia, MENA and LatAm: mine a region for DATA when it PRODUCES OR TRANSITS something the desk trades; mine it for STRATEGIES only when it TRADES what the desk trades, legally, with mandatory disclosure. Japan is the only region scoring on both columns -- retail FX is legal, enormous, MT5-native, and TFX publishes exchange data. China, Chile, Peru, Brazil, Dubai and Turkey are PRODUCERS: take the data, never the strategies, because nothing there trades this desk's venue. Russia/CIS is the one corpus worth mining for mechanisms without a data claim, because it is the largest MT5 corpus in the world and its authors trade this same terminal. SE Asian and MENA retail crowds have no disclosure: mechanisms only, claims never. NO_TABLE IS A ROUTE PROBLEM, NOT A PARSER PROBLEM. A JavaScript-rendered statistics portal serves an empty shell to a fetcher; its data lives at a JSON endpoint the page calls. Auto-discovery from the saved HTML does not find these -- the endpoints are in JS bundles, not the page -- so the remedy is a DECLARED url per source, verified once with a real request. cfets_fixing was fixed this way on 2026-09-15; abs_trade, boj_timeseries and krx_open_api were probed and returned 404/404/403, so they stay NO_TABLE rather than carrying an invented address.
boundary: THE FIVE REFUSED ACTS, AND NOTHING ELSE (LAWS 5e, principal 2026-09-23). Nothing here steals a credential or logs in as somebody else, bypasses an access control or a paywall, carries material non-public information, uses stolen or leaked private data, or harvests personal data. Everything else publicly visible is mined and tested. Licence, terms, robots and source class are ROUTING AND PROVENANCE LABELS -- they say what the desk may REDISTRIBUTE and how much weight the evidence carries, never whether it may be read. THIS LINE REPLACED A `PUBLIC OR LICENSED ONLY` BOUNDARY that predated the law and was a discovery brake of exactly the kind LAWS 5e names as deleted. `access` still declares what each ground needs, and a keyed or paid source with no key configured reports UNCONFIGURED -- never a failed probe, and never a silent skip.

cn_hard.name: China official, exchange and physical
cn_hard.why: the number itself is the observation: inventories, receipts, member positioning, fixings, settlement flow. This is the surface almost nobody joins together correctly, and it is where an information advantage is actually available to a public-data desk.

cn_aggregator.name: China aggregation APIs
cn_aggregator.why: discovery and prototyping speed. An aggregator is a convenience over the exchange, never an authority: where a direct exchange route exists it is preferred, because an aggregator's silent schema change is indistinguishable from a quiet market.

jp.name: Japan official and exchange
jp.why: Japan is the LARGEST RETAIL FX MARKET IN THE WORLD, it is MT4/MT5-native, and it trades the desk's own instruments -- JPY crosses, XAUUSD, indices. That is the transferability test Chinese rebar strategies fail and Japan passes: data ABOUT THE DESK'S OWN INSTRUMENTS. JPY crosses and financing costs are what Japan is for.

kr.name: Korea exchange and macro
kr.why: exports and semiconductors are a clean read on Asian industrial demand, and KRX publishes investor-type flow.

hk_sg.name: Hong Kong and Singapore
hk_sg.why: HK is the CN/offshore transmission point and HKMA's open interface needs no registration at all; Singapore carries the Asian commodity and freight trade.

tw.name: Taiwan
tw.why: semiconductor and trade information, and a second read on the same Asian industrial state.

genome.name: Public trader genome
genome.why: NOT for copying anyone. The question is structural: across tens of thousands of publicly observable strategies, what characteristics predict persistence AFTER costs. The graveyards are the valuable half -- a leaderboard of survivors answers a question nobody asked.

alt.name: Alternative and narrative
alt.why: trade, shipping, energy, weather and attention. Weakest priors here, so the highest bar.

physical.name: Physical commodity and production exhaust
physical.why: the market that exists BEFORE the price reacts. Inventories, deliveries, port cargo, rail freight and production are the physical balance the futures curve is an opinion about. This is the deepest public layer where a public-data desk can still be early.

participant.name: Exchange participant microdata
participant.why: member long/short rankings, OI change, concentration and option IV. CONCENTRATION, not net position, is what predicts a squeeze -- and the Chinese exchanges publish it while no Western feed carries it.

supply_chain.name: Corporate and procurement exhaust
supply_chain.why: tenders, hiring, land, permits, supplier graphs. An industrial-demand read built from operations rather than from a price. Mostly licensed rather than free, so each entry must earn its rent.

geospatial.name: Satellite and geospatial
geospatial.why: atmospheric and thermal observation over known industrial clusters, which is production measured directly rather than surveyed. Weakest prior of any plane and the highest bar: a fire is not a factory and an emissions anomaly is not output until it is shown to lead one.

search.name: Search and consumer attention
search.why: ACCELERATION, never level. Attention is a state variable that marks the crowded end of a move; the level is a popularity contest.

customs_micro.name: Customs microdata
customs_micro.why: commodity x country x customs point x transport mode, rather than a headline monthly total. Granularity is the whole edge: an aggregate that everyone has is not information.

logistics.name: Shipping, freight and port
logistics.why: freight is physical trade volume priced in real time, weeks upstream of the customs print it will eventually appear in.

scheduled_flow.name: Scheduled mechanical flows
scheduled_flow.why: A flow that is ANNOUNCED IN ADVANCE, dated, and executed mechanically is the rarest thing on this desk: a conditioner that is KNOWN BEFORE IT HAPPENS. Almost every other family here infers a state from price and hopes the inference holds. These do not need to be predicted at all -- only sized. Expect small effects and take them: they are independent of every price-pattern family in the book, which is what breadth is.

ru.name: Russia / CIS
ru.why: MetaQuotes is Russian-origin and the mql5.com community's centre of gravity is Russian-speaking, which makes this the LARGEST MT5 CORPUS IN THE WORLD -- and the only large one written by people trading the same terminal, the same brokers and the same instruments as this desk. `world_frontier._VOCAB` already carries the Russian vocabulary; nothing pointed at the ground.

physical_gold.name: Gold physical chokepoints
physical_gold.why: The book is gold-heavy and sees none of the physical side. Swiss refineries sit between London and Asia, so Swiss customs is the transit itself rather than a proxy for it, and LBMA vault holdings are the London float the Shanghai premium is measured against.

latam.name: South America -- the supply side
latam.why: the strategy corpus is thin and the ground is hostile to offshore FX, but South America PRODUCES what this desk trades. Chile is roughly a quarter of world copper; Peru is second; Brazil dominates coffee and sugar and ships iron ore. That is a data region, not a strategy region, and the routing rule says so explicitly.

oceania.name: Oceania -- and the desk's own venue
oceania.why: THE ONLY REGION THAT SCORES ON BOTH COLUMNS OF THE ROUTING RULE, and the one this desk's own broker is licensed in. Australia produces iron ore, coal, LNG and gold; New Zealand's dairy auctions are a scheduled, pre-announced flow into a currency the book holds sleeves in; and AUD is the CHINA PROXY CURRENCY, which closes the loop on the whole China plane -- GACC iron ore imports into Australian export receipts into AUD, one chain with both ends free. Sydney's Monday open (Sunday 21:00 UTC) is also the start of the FX week and the reopen gap the desk has never studied.

venue.name: The desk's own broker, by regulatory mandate
venue.why: Fusion Markets is ASIC-regulated, so it is legally REQUIRED to publish how it fills this account. The desk has been inferring execution semantics from 52 fill records that its counterparty had already written down in English. This is the densest unread document about the desk's actual trading environment and it outranks every dataset in the registry.

india.name: India -- the second gold consumer and a live USD cross
india.why: India held ZERO grounds in the attribution index while being the world's second largest physical gold consumer and the source of a USDINR the venue quotes. It is a PRODUCER/CONSUMER region under the routing rule: take the customs, central-bank and exchange data, never the retail strategy corpus, because offshore FX is not legal there and nothing in that crowd trades this venue.

north_america.name: North America -- the jurisdiction the desk's own quote currency belongs to
north_america.why: THE HIGHEST-PRIORITY DATA REGION AND IT HELD ZERO GROUNDS. Every symbol in the book is quoted against USD or hedged through it; the CFTC positioning report, the Fed's own balance sheet and rate releases, EIA inventories, COMEX warehouse stocks and USDA supply/demand are the primary observations behind gold, oil, gas, the softs and every FX cross the desk trades. This is a DATA region of the first rank and a strategy region of none -- US retail commentary is not mined for mechanisms here, the hard releases are.

institutional.name: Global / institutional -- the cross-jurisdiction observers
institutional.why: Bodies with no jurisdiction of their own that measure ALL of them: BIS policy rates and effective exchange rates, IMF reserves and commodity prices, the World Gold Council's demand and ETF flows, OPEC and IEA oil balances, the World Bank commodity sheet. These are the only series that are point-in-time comparable ACROSS regions, which is what makes a cross-regional mechanism testable at all. The index could not name this region.

mena.name: MENA -- the marginal barrel and two live USD crosses
mena.why: A PRODUCER region under the routing rule: Aramco's official selling prices and JODI's submissions are the supply side of the oil the desk trades, and CBRT's reserve and rate series drive a USDTRY the venue quotes. The retail crowds here carry no disclosure, so this is mechanisms and data only, claims never.

sea.name: South-East Asia -- palm, coffee, coal and the ASEAN crosses
sea.why: SE Asia held one ground. It PRODUCES palm oil (Malaysia/Indonesia), robusta coffee (Vietnam), thermal coal and LNG, and its central banks publish the series behind USDSGD, USDTHB, USDMYR and USDIDR. Data region, never a strategy region: no disclosure regime covers its retail crowds.

africa.name: Africa -- cocoa, PGMs and the gold-linked currencies
africa.why: Africa held one ground while supplying about two thirds of the world's cocoa (Cote d'Ivoire and Ghana), nearly all of its platinum and palladium, and the gold behind a ZAR the book holds sleeves in. Pure producer data.

sources.why: the desk's param-hash quota catches the same parameters on different symbols. It does NOT catch different symbols that are the same underlying, which is what a currency peg makes them

sources.name: Fusion Markets Product Disclosure Statement
sources.mechanism: READ 2026-09-15, 35 pages. It states outright that every product is entered into by Fusion AS PRINCIPAL and that Fusion MAKES A MARKET in its products; that all Stop-loss Orders are subject to agreement by Fusion, which has ABSOLUTE DISCRETION whether to accept one; and that Stop-loss Orders may not be executed at all. The counterparty is the house, not an exchange, and stop acceptance is discretionary by contract
sources.why: this changes the interpretation of the desk's own TOUCHED finding. unfilled_fork attributed every touched-but-unfilled order to queue position, latency or stop distance -- an exchange's vocabulary for a dealer's venue. Dealer discretion is a documented fourth cause and is now named in the verdict

sources.name: Fusion Markets Hedging Counterparty Policy (ASIC)
sources.mechanism: READ 2026-09-15. 'Not all client transactions are hedged on a back-to-back basis so we may have a net position in markets that we offer.' Flow is INTERNALISED in part, with volume among the factors deciding whether a given order is hedged out
sources.why: if the broker internalises, the desk's counterparty is the house on that flow, which is the premise behind every execution-quality question it has been asking

sources.name: Ukrainian Ministry of Agrarian Policy export data
sources.mechanism: grain corridor volumes are a supply series with a political clock; the weekly export pace is the observable

sources.name: SOCAR and Azerbaijani state statistics
sources.mechanism: BTC pipeline throughput and Shah Deniz gas are the Caspian supply leg into the European balance, outside Russian transit

sources.name: Kazakhstan Bureau of National Statistics energy series
sources.mechanism: Tengiz and Kashagan production and the CPC export volume -- a Brent-grade supply leg and a large copper producer in one statistical office

sources.name: IBGE Brazilian statistics -- CPI, production, agriculture
sources.mechanism: the crop survey is the production forecast CONAB is measured against, and IPCA is the rate the central bank responds to

sources.name: UNICA sugarcane crush and sugar/ethanol mix
sources.mechanism: the fortnightly crush report names the sugar-versus-ethanol allocation, which is the single largest swing factor in world sugar supply and ties it to the oil price

sources.name: CECAFE Brazilian green coffee export statistics
sources.mechanism: monthly arabica export tonnage from the dominant producer, published ahead of the ICO aggregate

sources.name: SECEX weekly Brazilian trade balance
sources.mechanism: a WEEKLY trade balance is unusual and valuable: it prices the real's terms of trade four times a month instead of once

sources.name: Banco de la Republica Colombia statistics
sources.mechanism: a coffee and crude exporter's reserve and rate series; the Colombian coffee federation's price is set against this FX

sources.name: INDEC Argentina trade and agricultural exports
sources.mechanism: Argentina is the largest soybean-meal exporter; the export-tax regime makes farmer selling lumpy and the registration data shows it

sources.name: RBA monetary policy decisions and minutes
sources.mechanism: the scheduled rate event in the desk's own broker's jurisdiction and the currency the book holds the most crosses in

sources.name: ABS consumer price index and labour force
sources.mechanism: the quarterly CPI is the single largest scheduled AUD repricing; the monthly indicator now lands between them

sources.name: Pilbara Ports / Port Hedland monthly throughput
sources.mechanism: roughly half the world's seaborne iron ore leaves through one port, and it publishes the tonnage monthly -- the supply side the Chinese port inventory reads at the other end

sources.name: Stats NZ overseas merchandise trade
sources.mechanism: dairy is roughly a quarter of New Zealand's exports; the monthly trade release is the kiwi's terms of trade with a two-week lag on the GDT auction

sources.name: AEMO gas and electricity market data
sources.mechanism: east-coast gas prices and LNG netbacks; Australian LNG competes directly with Qatari and US cargoes into the same Asian buyers

sources.name: ADNOC Murban crude and IFAD exchange data
sources.mechanism: Murban is now an exchange-traded benchmark; its spread to Brent and Dubai is the Gulf's own light-sour pricing signal

sources.name: Iraq SOMO export volumes and official selling prices
sources.mechanism: OPEC's second largest producer publishes its liftings monthly, which is compliance measured at the loading terminal rather than by secondary sources

sources.name: TurkStat trade, CPI and gold import statistics
sources.mechanism: Turkish gold imports spike when the lira devalues -- the two series in one office, which is a mechanism the desk can test directly

sources.name: Borsa Istanbul precious metals market data
sources.mechanism: the lira-gold quote and its premium to the dollar price is the domestic hedging bid measured directly instead of inferred from imports

sources.name: Gas Exporting Countries Forum monthly gas market report
sources.mechanism: the LNG exporters' own balance, which is the supply-side counterpart to the European storage and Asian import series the desk already reads

sources.name: ICCO quarterly bulletin of cocoa statistics
sources.mechanism: the global grind and the surplus/deficit estimate that the West African arrivals series is measured against; the two disagreeing is the tradable signal

sources.name: Bank of Ghana monetary and cocoa export series
sources.mechanism: Ghana is the second cocoa producer AND a large gold producer; the reserve series carries both and its gold-for-oil programme is an explicit official flow

sources.name: GASC Egyptian wheat tender results
sources.mechanism: the world's largest wheat buyer tenders publicly; the awarded price and origin is a direct, dated demand observation that the futures market trades around

sources.name: Central Bank of Kenya statistics and horticulture exports
sources.mechanism: tea and coffee export earnings and the shilling; the Mombasa auction clears against this FX and the two together are the East African soft complex

sources.name: DGCIS monthly commodity-wise import detail
sources.mechanism: the audited customs line behind the headline trade number, split by commodity -- the gold tonnage the GJEPC and press numbers are estimates of

sources.name: IBJA daily domestic bullion reference rates
sources.mechanism: the domestic rate versus the landed import parity is the Indian physical premium or discount, which is the demand signal at daily frequency rather than monthly

sources.name: NSDL FPI debt utilisation and limits
sources.mechanism: the debt-limit utilisation is a capacity constraint on the largest scheduled inflow; it caps how much of an index-inclusion flow can actually arrive

sources.name: GAPKI Indonesian palm oil production and stocks
sources.mechanism: the Indonesian half of world palm supply, which MPOB's Malaysian series cannot see; the export-levy and domestic-obligation policy moves it in steps

sources.name: Thai Ministry of Commerce rice and rubber exports
sources.mechanism: Thailand is a top sugar and rice exporter; the export-price series is the baht's soft commodity terms of trade

sources.name: MPA Singapore bunker sales and vessel arrivals
sources.mechanism: the world's largest bunkering port publishes monthly fuel sales -- marine fuel demand measured at the pump, which is the residual leg of the crude balance

sources.name: Swiss National Bank data portal
sources.mechanism: sight deposits are the SNB's intervention footprint published weekly, and Switzerland is the refining chokepoint the desk already reads through customs

sources.name: Destatis German trade, CPI and production
sources.mechanism: German industrial production is the euro area's cycle and its gas intensity is the channel a European energy shock takes into EURUSD

sources.name: ONS UK CPI, labour market and trade
sources.mechanism: the scheduled inflation and wage prints that set Bank Rate and therefore the sterling carry the book holds crosses in

sources.name: Institut National de la Statistique Cote d'Ivoire trade series
sources.mechanism: the audited export value behind the Conseil Cafe-Cacao's weekly arrivals; the two series disagreeing is a smuggling or grading signal the London contract prices

sources.name: Bank of Tanzania and East African mineral export statistics
sources.mechanism: East African artisanal and mine gold exports are a supply leg outside South Africa, and the central bank's own purchase programme is an official bid on it

CN_HARD_DATA.why: official, exchange, physical and flow. Exhaust this before a single social post is read: the hard surfaces carry the information and the forums carry opinions about it.

CN_DEEP_FOREST.why: already built and already running over 30 Chinese grounds. This registry does NOT duplicate it -- a second crawler over the same ground would double the trial charge and halve the attention.

JP_INTELLIGENCE.why: Japan is the only Asian country where retail FX is legal, enormous, MT5-native, trades the desk's own instruments AND publishes structured exchange data. TFX swap points check the desk's own financing model; TFX open interest is retail positioning on pairs the book already holds. Both are data ABOUT THE DESK'S OWN INSTRUMENTS, which is the transferability test a Chinese rebar strategy fails.

KR_INTELLIGENCE.why: KRX participant data and the 20-day export print

HK_SG_INTELLIGENCE.why: the offshore transmission point and the regional trade cycle

GLOBAL_TRADER_GENOME.why: structure that predicts persistence after costs, learned from graveyards as much as from survivors

ALT_DATA_FOREST.why: trade, shipping, energy and attention. Weakest priors, highest bar.

CN_PHYSICAL.why: the physical economy and the participants holding it: the market that exists before the price reacts

SUPPLY_CHAIN_EXHAUST.why: tenders, hiring, land, permits and supplier graphs fused into an industrial-demand read built from operations rather than price

GEOSPATIAL.why: observation and attention. Weakest priors of anything here, so the highest bar and a residual-after-controls discipline

RU_CIS.why: the largest MT5 corpus in the world, on the same terminal and instruments this desk trades. The Russian vocabulary is already wired in world_frontier._VOCAB and nothing pointed at it.

SCHEDULED_FLOW.why: flows announced before they execute. The only conditioners on this desk that do not have to be predicted, only sized -- and independent of every price-pattern family in the book.

PHYSICAL_GOLD.why: the book is gold-heavy and sees none of the physical side: Swiss transit and the London float, against the Shanghai premium that is already wired.

LATAM_SUPPLY.why: a DATA region under the routing rule: it produces copper, silver, coffee, sugar and iron ore that this desk trades through currencies and metals. No strategy mining -- offshore FX is restricted there and the corpus is thin.

OCEANIA.why: the only region scoring on BOTH columns of the routing rule, and AUD is the China proxy currency that closes the China chain.

VENUE_TERMS.why: the broker's own ASIC-mandated disclosures. Execution semantics the desk was inferring from 52 fill records, written down and binding.
